description: CI/CD pipeline definition files (.gitlab-ci.yml, .github/workflows/*.yml, Jenkinsfile, .travis.yml, and similar) are directly reachable over HTTP from the deployed application.
impact: Reveals the build and deployment pipeline in detail — internal hostnames, deployment targets, build steps, and occasionally hardcoded secrets or tokens that should have used the CI system's secret store instead — giving an attacker a map of the deployment process and potential additional credentials.
remediation: Ensure CI/CD configuration files are never placed inside, or reachable from, the public web root — they belong in the repository root or .github/.gitlab directories, not the deployed artifact.
Never hardcode secrets directly in pipeline YAML — use the CI platform's secret/variable store instead.
Add an explicit deny rule for common CI config filenames at the web server level as defense in depth.

audience_guidance.student: CI/CD config files tell an automated system how to build and deploy an app. They're meant to live in the source repository, not be served to website visitors — if they are, an attacker gets a detailed map of how deployment works, and sometimes even leftover secrets.
audience_guidance.developer: Double-check your build process only copies application files into the deployed artifact, not the whole repository — and never hardcode secrets in pipeline YAML, use your CI platform's secret store instead.
audience_guidance.bug_bounty_hunter: Check common CI config paths directly (/.github/workflows/, /Jenkinsfile, /.gitlab-ci.yml) — an exposed one is a good lead for further recon, and occasionally contains a usable credential.
audience_guidance.pentester: Use any exposed pipeline config to map internal hostnames and deployment targets, and check for hardcoded secrets that shouldn't be there.
audience_guidance.security_team: Include exposed CI/CD configuration in routine external exposure scans, and audit pipeline definitions for hardcoded secrets that should be migrated to the CI platform's secret store.
